Diagram editing screens

Every screen and state for DGM-14, drawn at real sizes (desktop 1280 × 800, phone 390 × 844, panels and dialogs at their own size). Nothing here is built; these are for approval before any UI code (ADR-011). Sources: docs/29-DIAGRAMMING.md, ADR-045, 046 and 047, and the design’s §7 and §10.

What stays the same. The board block, its toolbar and menu, and everyone else’s view are unchanged. Diagram mode is per person and per board: one new button on the block opens that board full screen with shape libraries, ports, routing, layout and properties.

Examples are realistic: a checkout platform’s service map (gateway, load balancer, services, Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL), an orders database schema, and an order domain model in UML. All colours are OpenCanvas tokens; all icons are Lucide. Use the switch above for light and dark.

Decisions for the owner are marked Decision in the notes: the labelled Diagram button (1a), board names (1d), BPMN on or off by default (2f), Esc to leave (5d), keeping bends in auto-layout (6a), soft or hard size limit (9b) and the deleted-shape outline (10b).

S1 · Entering and leaving diagram mode ADR-045 §8: per board

Diagram mode is something one person opens on one board. It does not change the document, the board block or anyone else’s view. The block gets one new control; everything else in the whiteboard stays as it is today.

S2 · Shapes panel Registry: data only

A compact panel on the left. Libraries come from the declarative registry (ADR-045 §3): names, glyphs, default size and ports, no code. Search covers names and keywords across all libraries. Each tile shows a real preview of the shape, not an icon of it. Crops are at real size (256 px wide).

S3 · Canvas ADR-046 SVG · ADR-047 routing

The canvas keeps the board’s SVG renderer (ADR-046). Additions: a line grid with major lines every 100 px, rulers that mark the selection, snapping with guides, ports, port-to-port connectors, routing around shapes, editable bends, multi-select, containers and the minimap. The example is a real checkout platform: gateway, load balancer, three services, a Kafka topic, a cache and two databases.

S4 · Properties panel props: merged per field

The right panel shows what is selected, in plain sections. Every field is one entry in the shape’s props, so two people editing different fields of the same shape both keep their change (ADR-045, owner condition). Lists (attributes, methods, columns) reorder by dragging the grip or with ⌥↑ / ⌥↓.

S5 · Outline, commands and keyboard WCAG 2.2 AA

Everything on the canvas can be reached without a pointer: the outline lists every shape in order, Commands runs any action by name, and connectors can be drawn from the keyboard. Focus is always visible (2.5 px accent ring, at least 3:1 against the canvas in both themes), and the canvas announces what has focus.

S6 · Auto-layout ADR-047 §5

Layout never runs on its own. It is an explicit action with a preview; applying it writes every new position in one transaction, so one Undo puts everything back. It runs in the background (Dagre first) and never blocks typing.

S7 · Import and export FC-10 pipeline · SEC-39

Mermaid and draw.io join the approved import dialog (FC-10: 640 px, same steps). Every import is a dry run first: a report of what converts and what doesn’t, before anything is added. Every export to another tool says what changes. Imported files are untrusted: sizes, XML depth and entities are checked, links and scripts are removed.

S8 · Shapes this app can’t draw ADR-045 §3–5

Two cases from the registry lookup. A kind whose library is missing draws as its base shape with a small plugin marker. A type this app doesn’t know at all becomes a placeholder box. In both, the box can be moved, resized, connected and deleted, every other field is kept untouched, and the panel explains it in one paragraph.

S9 · Size budget ADR-045 §7: 25 % of max_doc_bytes

A board may use a quarter of the document limit (5 MB of 20 MB by default). The diagram warns at 80 % and again when over. Counting is done by the client from the board’s encoded size, so it needs no server change. Example: a large platform network, zoomed out to 15 %.

S10 · Working together Yjs · awareness · ADR-045 §6

Selections, cursors, hover and drag previews travel as presence, never as document data. Edits merge per field. The two awkward cases are designed explicitly: someone deletes a shape you are connecting to, and someone who can only view.

S11 · Phone (390 px) Viewing and light edits

On a phone the diagram opens full screen without side panels or rulers. People can view, pan and zoom, select, rename, recolour, move, add a shape (optionally connected to the selected one), connect two shapes and delete. Large-diagram authoring stays desktop-first: auto-layout, import, bend editing and long property lists say “larger screen” instead of half-working.
